content: Though the above test is already more indicative of policy performance on real users than measuring statistical metrics of user behaviour, a better test is to test with human users. For the test on human users, two policies for each US that was used for training are chosen from the five policies. The first policy is the one that performed best when tested on the NUS. The second is the one that performed best when tested on the ABUS. This choice of policies is motivated by a type of overfitting to be seen in Sec. SECREF17 . The evaluation of the trained dialogue policies in interaction with real users follows a similar set-up to BIBREF40 . Users are recruited through the Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) service. 1000 dialogues (250 per policy) were gathered. The learnt policies were incorporated into an SDS pipeline with a commercial ASR system. The AMT users were asked to find a restaurant that matches certain constraints and find certain requests. Subjects were randomly allocated to one of the four analysed systems. After each dialogue the users were asked whether they judged the dialogue to be successful or not which was then translated to the reward measure.
